easy.def: An empty room or job that is free to take.
examples: The hotel has a vacancy.
A job vacancy.
No vacancy.

more.def: A room or a job that is empty and available for someone to take.
examples: The sign said "Vacancy," so we knew the hotel had a free room.
There is a vacancy for a teacher at our school.
The motel had no vacancy.

easy.def: Empty and not being used.
examples: The seat is vacant.
A vacant house.
The room was vacant.

more.def: Empty and not being used or lived in by anyone.
examples: There was a vacant seat in the front row, so I sat down.
The old house on the corner has been vacant for years.
A vacant lot beside the school became a community garden.

easy.def: To leave a place and make it empty.
examples: Vacate the room.
They vacated the house.
Please vacate your seat.

more.def: To leave a place, such as a room or a seat, so that it is empty for someone else.
examples: The guests must vacate the room by noon.
Please vacate your seat for the next rider.
The family vacated the house after the flood.

easy.def: A time when you rest and do not go to school or work.
examples: We went to the beach on vacation.
No school! It is summer vacation.
We took a vacation to see Grandma.

more.def: A time of rest away from school or work, often spent on a trip.
examples: Our family spent summer vacation camping in the mountains.
He sent a postcard while on vacation in Italy.
The store owner is taking a week of vacation.

easy.def: To give a shot that helps protect from illness.
examples: The nurse will vaccinate me.
We vaccinated the dog.
They vaccinate kids at school.

more.def: To give a person or animal a shot that protects against a disease.
examples: The nurse vaccinated all the students.
The vet vaccinated our puppy.
Doctors vaccinate children against many diseases.

easy.def: A shot that helps keep you from getting sick.
examples: I got a vaccination.
A vaccination is a shot.
The nurse gave me a vaccination.

more.def: A shot given to protect people from a certain illness.
examples: I got a vaccination before the school year began.
The nurse gave each child a vaccination.
A vaccination helps your body fight germs.

easy.def: A shot that helps keep you from getting sick.
examples: I got a vaccine.
The vaccine keeps me safe.
The nurse gave me a vaccine.

more.def: A medicine, often given as a shot, that helps your body fight a certain disease so that you do not get it.
examples: The nurse gave me a vaccine to protect me from the flu.
A vaccine helps your body learn how to fight a germ.
Scientists worked hard to make a vaccine for the disease.

easy.def: A machine that cleans floors.
examples: Dad uses the vacuum.
The vacuum is loud.
I turned on the vacuum.

more.def: A machine that cleans by sucking up dust and dirt.
examples: Dad pushed the vacuum across the carpet.
The vacuum cleaner picked up the crumbs.
I put the vacuum away.

easy.def: A space with no air in it.
examples: Space is a vacuum.
There is no sound in a vacuum.
A vacuum has no air.

more.def: A space that has no air or other matter in it.
examples: Space is nearly a vacuum.
Sound cannot travel in a vacuum.
The jar was a vacuum with the air pumped out.

easy.def: Not clear or not exact.
examples: I have a vague memory of that day.
His answer was vague.
The map was vague.

more.def: Not clear or exact, so that you are not sure about the details.
examples: The teacher gave only vague directions, so we got lost.
I have a vague memory of visiting the farm when I was three.
The shape in the fog was vague, and we could not tell what it was.

easy.def: Too proud of how you look.
examples: The vain prince looked in the mirror.
She is vain.
A vain peacock.

more.def: Having too high an opinion of yourself, especially of how you look.
examples: The vain prince looked in the mirror all day.
The vain peacock showed off its tail.
He was too vain to wear a hat.

easy.def: Without success.
examples: Their efforts were in vain.
The vain attempt failed.
We tried in vain.

more.def: Having no result, or failing to work.
examples: They tried in vain to open the stuck door.
Her vain attempt to reach the shelf failed.
The effort was in vain.

easy.def: Brave and strong.
examples: The valiant knight rode on.
A valiant try.
The valiant firefighter helped.

more.def: Showing great courage.
examples: The valiant knight rode toward the castle.
We made a valiant effort to climb the hill.
The valiant firefighter ran into the building to help.

easy.def: Right or good enough to be accepted.
examples: Your ticket is valid.
That is a valid answer.
She had a valid reason.

more.def: Acceptable because it is correct, fair or allowed by the rules.
examples: A ticket is only valid for the day printed on it.
Tom had a valid reason for being late, since the bus broke down.
Your library card is valid for one more year.

easy.def: Low land between hills or mountains.
examples: The village is in a valley.
A river runs through the valley.
We looked down at the valley.

more.def: An area of low land between hills or mountains, often with a river.
examples: The farm sat in a green valley between two mountains.
A river carved the valley over millions of years.
Fog filled the valley each morning.

easy.def: Worth a lot.
examples: The gold ring is valuable.
Clean water is valuable.
This old coin is valuable.

more.def: Worth a lot of money, or very important and useful.
examples: Her advice was valuable because it helped me solve the problem.
A good friend is more valuable than gold.
The painting is too valuable to hang in the hallway.

easy.def: Things that cost a lot of money.
examples: Put your valuables in the safe.
She locked up her valuables.
Do not lose your valuables.

more.def: Items that are worth a lot of money or are very important to you.
examples: The hotel keeps guests' valuables in a safe.
She packed her jewelry and other valuables in a small bag.
Leave your valuables at home when you go to the beach.

easy.def: How much something is worth.
examples: The coin has great value.
The value of the house.
The value is ten dollars.

more.def: The amount of money that something is worth.
examples: The old coin has great value.
The value of the painting is high.
She checked the value of the stamp.

easy.def: How important something is.
examples: Friends have great value.
I see the value in practice.
Kindness has value.

more.def: How important or useful something is.
examples: I see the value in practicing every day.
A good friend has great value.
The value of exercise is clear.

easy.def: A part that opens and shuts to let water through.
examples: Turn the valve.
The valve is closed.
The valve controls the water.

more.def: A part that opens and shuts to control the flow of water, air or gas.
examples: Dad turned the valve to turn off the water.
The valve on the tire lets air in.
The heart has valves that keep blood moving.

easy.def: A pretend creature in scary stories.
examples: He dressed as a vampire for Halloween.
A vampire wears a cape.
The vampire in the movie was pretend.

more.def: A creature in scary stories that is said to sleep in a coffin by day and come out at night.
examples: The vampire in the story wore a black cape.
Kids dressed as vampires and witches at the Halloween party.
Vampires are make-believe, so there is nothing to fear.

easy.def: A person who breaks or paints on things that are not theirs.
examples: A vandal broke the sign.
Vandals hurt the park.
The vandal was sorry.

more.def: A person who damages property that belongs to others on purpose.
examples: A vandal sprayed paint on the park bench.
Vandals broke the swings, so the park was closed.
The town asked the vandal to help clean up.

easy.def: To break or spoil things on purpose.
examples: Do not vandalize the wall.
Someone vandalized the sign.
It is wrong to vandalize.

more.def: To damage or spoil public or private property on purpose.
examples: It is wrong to vandalize a school.
Someone vandalized the park bench with paint.
Town workers cleaned the sign that was vandalized.

easy.def: A sweet flavor used in ice cream and cakes.
examples: I like vanilla ice cream.
The cake tastes like vanilla.
Mom added vanilla.

more.def: A sweet flavor that comes from the pod of a tropical plant, used in cakes, ice cream and other foods.
examples: I like vanilla ice cream with chocolate sauce.
Mom added a spoonful of vanilla to the cake batter.
The cookies have a warm vanilla smell.

easy.def: To go away so no one can see it.
examples: The magician made the coin vanish.
The fog will vanish soon.
My cookie vanished!

more.def: To disappear suddenly or completely.
examples: The deer vanished into the forest before I could take a picture.
The rainbow vanished when the sun went behind a cloud.
Her smile vanished when she heard the news.

easy.def: Going away until it cannot be seen.
examples: The vanishing mist went away.
He did a vanishing trick.
The vanishing cat disappeared.

more.def: Disappearing or becoming rare.
examples: The magician performed a vanishing trick with a coin.
The vanishing mist faded as the sun came up.
The white rhino is a vanishing species.

easy.def: To beat someone or something completely.
examples: The hero vanquished the dragon.
The team vanquished its rival.
She vanquished her fear of swimming.

more.def: To defeat someone or something completely.
examples: The knight in the story vanquished the dragon and saved the village.
Our team vanquished its old rivals in the championship game.
With practice, she vanquished her fear of speaking to a crowd.

easy.def: A thin gas or mist.
examples: Steam is vapor.
Vapor rose from the soup.
I saw vapor.

more.def: A thin, cloudy gas, such as steam or mist, made from a liquid.
examples: Vapor rose from the hot soup.
Water vapor forms clouds in the sky.
A mist of vapor rose from the pond in the morning.

easy.def: To turn into steam or gas.
examples: Water will vaporize when it boils.
The heat vaporized the water.
Alcohol vaporizes.

more.def: To change from a liquid or solid into a gas.
examples: Water vaporizes when it boils.
The heat vaporized the puddle.
The sun vaporized the morning dew.

easy.def: Likely to change.
examples: The weather is variable.
A variable speed.
Prices are variable.

more.def: Likely to change or able to be changed.
examples: The weather in spring is variable, with sun one minute and rain the next.
The fan has a variable speed that you can set high or low.
The price of fruit is variable throughout the year.

easy.def: A thing in math or science that can change.
examples: The letter x is a variable.
A variable can change.
Change the variable.

more.def: A letter or a thing in math or a science test that can change or take different values.
examples: In math, the letter x is a variable that stands for a number.
In our plant experiment, the amount of water was the variable.
A scientist changes only one variable at a time.

easy.def: A small change or a different kind.
examples: The song has a variation.
A variation of the game.
There is a variation in size.

more.def: A change or a difference from what is usual, or a different form of the same thing.
examples: The musician played a variation of the tune with a faster beat.
There is a lot of variation in the size of the dogs at the park.
Her recipe is a variation of my grandmother's.

easy.def: Many different kinds.
examples: The store has a variety of toys.
I like variety.
A variety of fruits.

more.def: A mix of many different kinds of things.
examples: The pet shop sells a variety of birds.
We ate a variety of fruits at the picnic.
The garden had a great variety of flowers.

easy.def: Many different kinds.
examples: The shop sells various toys.
We saw various bugs in the yard.
The crayons come in various colors.

more.def: Of several different kinds.
examples: The garden has flowers of various colors and sizes.
People came to the fair from various towns.
There are various ways to solve this problem.

easy.def: A clear coating that makes wood shiny.
examples: The table has varnish.
The varnish is shiny.
Dad put varnish on the chair.

more.def: A clear liquid painted on wood that dries to a hard, shiny layer.
examples: Varnish protects the wooden floor from scratches.
The varnish made the table shine.
The wood was finished with clear varnish.

easy.def: To cover with a clear, shiny coat.
examples: Varnish the table.
He varnished the door.
She will varnish the box.

more.def: To paint a clear, hard coat onto wood.
examples: He varnished the old table.
She varnished the wooden box.
They varnished the boat.

easy.def: To be different from time to time.
examples: The weather can vary each day.
Our lunches vary from day to day.
Prices vary from store to store.

more.def: To change or to be different from one another, often depending on the time or place.
examples: Sizes of dogs vary a lot, from tiny to huge.
The temperature varies from morning to night in the desert.
Her moods varied, so we never knew what to expect.

easy.def: Different from one to another.
examples: We have varying sizes.
Varying colors.
The varying heights of the trees.

more.def: Changing or different from one to another.
examples: The shop has hats in varying sizes.
The varying heights of the trees made a pretty skyline.
We had varying amounts of rain each month.

easy.def: A tall container for holding flowers.
examples: She put flowers in a vase.
The vase is on the table.
The vase is full of roses.

more.def: A container, often made of glass or clay, that is used to hold flowers or for display.
examples: She put the tulips in a tall glass vase.
The vase fell off the shelf and cracked.
A blue vase full of daisies sat in the middle of the table.

easy.def: Very big.
examples: The desert is vast.
A vast ocean.
The field is vast.

more.def: Extremely large in size or amount.
examples: The desert is vast and empty.
A vast ocean lay before us.
The library has a vast collection of books.

easy.def: A large tank for holding liquid.
examples: A vat of paint.
The vat was full.
A giant vat.

more.def: A very large tank or container for holding liquids, such as in a factory.
examples: A giant vat of chocolate stirred in the candy factory.
The vat was filled with dye.
Workers poured the milk into a large vat.

easy.def: A strong room for keeping money or valuable things safe.
examples: The bank has a vault.
The money is in the vault.
The vault door is heavy.

more.def: A strong, locked room where money and valuable things are kept.
examples: The bank keeps its gold in a vault.
The vault door was thick and heavy.
Important papers are stored in a vault.

easy.def: To jump over something using your hands or a pole.
examples: He vaulted the fence.
She vaulted over the gate.
The athlete vaulted.

more.def: To jump over something by pushing off with your hands or a pole.
examples: He vaulted over the fence.
The athlete vaulted over the high bar with a pole.
She vaulted over a log.
